_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: even 0-based indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Index 0 is the bilingual cover, index 1 the Hindi General Instructions; every odd index 1-13 is Hindi. The alternating hypothesis HELD without exception on this paper: all seven odd-page TOPS were cropped and read individually and carry Hindi only - the English visible on them at thumbnail size is scanner show-through from the reverse of the sheet, and index 14 (the last page) is English, not blank. No English text sits on any odd page, so nothing was lost by reading the even ones. DECIMAL POINTS: the PAPER prints ORDINARY baseline full stops throughout (verified at 2.2x-2.4x magnification on '1.5', '0.6', '1.0', '2.0 and 1.0', '1.5 x 10^8'), so no \cdot is used anywhere. Its own MARKING SCHEME disagrees with it - the scheme prints RAISED dots in its worked algebra (0.6, 1.5, 0.248085) while using ordinary ones in its prose figures (3.5mm, 4.5mm, 931.5, 231.09). The paper is followed, per the brief. STRUCTURE: the printed General Instructions agree with the term2_sci table exactly - 12 questions, THREE sections, A = Q1-3 at 2 marks, B = Q4-11 at 3 marks, C = Q12 case study at 5 marks; 6 + 24 + 5 = 35. This paper prints SEVEN instructions, not the six the addendum records for Chemistry 2022: (vi) is the internal-choice line and (vii) is the log-tables line. Instruction (vi) gives NO COUNT ('internal choice has been provided in some of the questions'), so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme for a bare OR on its own line and confirming each against a printed OR / Hindi 'athava' on the page: THREE internal choices, at Q3, Q6 and Q7 - scheme ORs on ms p03, p05, p06; paper ORs on idx 4, 6, 8 with the Hindi counterparts on idx 3, 5, 7. Primary-branch marks sum to 35. SECTION-C KEYS: read by vision from ms p09, printed in the '(i)-a' convention - (i)-a (ii)-b (iii)-c (iv)-b (v)-b - and uppercased to A, B, C, B, B. All five were independently re-derived as a sanity check that the right option was matched and all five agree; no disagreement to record. 19 rows: 14 subjective + 5 mcq.

questions.stem:
(i) Define SI unit of power of a lens.
(ii) A plano convex lens is made of glass of refractive index 1.5. The radius of curvature of the convex surface is 25 cm.
(ii.i) Calculate the focal length of the lens.

A slit of width 0.6 mm is illuminated by a beam of light consisting of two wavelengths 600 nm and 480 nm. The diffraction pattern is observed on a screen 1.0 m from the slit. Find :
(i) The distance of the second bright fringe from the central maximum pertaining to light of 600 nm.
(ii) The least distance from the central maximum at which bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide.
questions._cbseVoided: (Note: Full credit for finding the position by taking n = 3 or n= 4 for n = 3, xn = 3.5mm and for n = 4 , xn, = 4.5mm)
questions._flag: ACCEPT-EITHER-ANSWER NOTE OUTSIDE SECTION A, of the dual-key shape, on sub-part (ii). This paper's marking scheme (ms p05) sets (2n+1) x 600 = (2n+3) x 480, reaches n = 3.5 - a non-integer fringe order, which cannot be a physical order - quotes x_n = 4 mm from it, and then awards full credit for EITHER n = 3 (3.5 mm) or n = 4 (4.5 mm). Three different positions are printed for one question, so there is no single official answer and a later authoring pass must not pick one silently. WORDING DIFFERS FROM THE OPENER AND IS TRANSCRIBED FROM MY OWN SCHEME: 55/5/2 prints 'Full credit for finding...' where the committed 55/5/1 prints 'Give full credit for finding...'. Verified at 2.6x magnification; the leading 'Give' is absent here. Everything else in the two notes agrees.

A ray of light passes through a prism of refractive index \(\sqrt{2}\) as shown in the figure. Find :
(i) The angle of incidence \((\angle r_2)\) at face AC.
(ii) The angle of minimum deviation for this prism.
questions._figure: REQUIRED - the stem says only 'as shown in the figure' and names no angle, so the prism's geometry and the ray's path both exist only in the drawing. Page idx 8. READ ON MY OWN PAGE at 2.6x, not copied from the opener. DESCRIBED (labelling and layout): a triangle drawn with its apex A at the top and its base running from B at the lower left to C at the lower right; an angle value is printed inside the apex at A and another inside the base angle at B; the label for the refractive index is printed inside the triangle near face AC; a ray arrives from the lower left carrying a direction arrowhead and meets face AB at a point labelled M; a second ray runs horizontally from M across the interior to a point labelled N on face AC, also carrying an arrowhead; short dotted normals are drawn at both M and N, the interior angle at M is labelled r1 and the interior angle at N is labelled r2, and a further dotted line runs outward beyond N. WITHHELD deliberately: what the ray does at face AC after N relative to that face, which is exactly what sub-part (i) tests, and the two printed angle VALUES, since sub-part (ii) turns on the apex angle. questions.stem:
(i) Draw V-I characteristics of a p-n Junction diode.
(ii) Differentiate between the threshold voltage and the breakdown voltage for a diode.
(iii) Write the property of a junction diode which makes it suitable for rectification of ac voltages.

In a fission event of \({}^{238}_{92}\mathrm{U}\) by fast moving neutrons, no neutrons are emitted and final products, after the beta decay of the primary fragments, are \({}^{140}_{58}\mathrm{Ce}\) and \({}^{99}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}\). Calculate Q for this process. Neglect the masses of electrons/positrons emitted during the intermediate steps.
Given : \(m\left({}^{238}_{92}\mathrm{U}\right) = 238.05079\mathrm{u};\ m\left({}^{140}_{58}\mathrm{Ce}\right) = 139.90543\mathrm{u}\)
\(m\left({}^{99}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}\right) = 98.90594\mathrm{u};\ m\left({}^{1}_{0}\mathrm{n}\right) = 1.008665\mathrm{u}\)
questions._cbseVoided: (Note: Award this 1 mark even if Q-value is not calculated)
questions._flag: UNCONDITIONAL AWARD-REGARDLESS NOTE OUTSIDE SECTION A, and a PARTIAL void: the marking scheme (ms p09) splits the 3 marks 2 for the mass defect + 1 for the Q value, then awards that 1 mark whether or not the final step was done. Recorded under _cbseVoided per the addendum's 'even if ... is not' wording rule, NOT under _flag alone. Corroborated by the paper itself: the constants block on page idx 2 lists c, h, e, mu_0, epsilon_0, 1/(4 pi epsilon_0), the electron, neutron and proton masses, Avogadro's number and the Boltzmann constant, and does NOT give 1 u = 931.5 MeV or any value for u - so a candidate cannot reach the scheme's own 231.09 MeV from the data printed, which is presumably why CBSE awarded the mark regardless (instruction 7 also forbids a calculator). The scheme's arithmetic is correct; this is a defect in the QUESTION PAPER's data, not in the key. The note wording is byte-identical to the committed opener's.

questions.context: A ray of light travels from a denser to a rarer medium. After refraction, it bends away from the normal. When we keep increasing the angle of incidence, the angle of refraction also increases till the refracted ray grazes along the interface of two media. The angle of incidence for which it happens is called critical angle. If the angle of incidence is increased farther the ray will not emerge and it will be reflected back in the denser medium. This phenomenon is called total internal reflection of light.
questions.stem: A ray of light travels from a medium into water at an angle of incidence of \(18^\circ\). The refractive index of the medium is more than that of water and the critical angle for the interface between the two media is \(20^\circ\). Which one of the following figures best represents the correct path of the ray of light ?

questions._figure: REQUIRED - THE FOUR OPTIONS ARE THEMSELVES DRAWINGS and the stem names none of them, so the whole discrimination lives in the figure. Page idx 12. READ ON MY OWN PAGE at 3x, not copied from the opener. DESCRIBED (the layout common to all four boxes, which is all that can be said safely): the four options are drawn as a 2x2 block of rectangular boxes, (A) and (B) on the upper row and (C) and (D) on the lower row, each label printed outside its box - (A) and (B) above, (C) and (D) below. Every box is divided by a single horizontal interface line; the region ABOVE the line is grey-shaded and carries the word WATER set in the shaded band at the left, and the region BELOW the line is unshaded. In each box a straight incident ray arrives from the lower left, carries a direction arrowhead, and meets the interface at a point roughly in the middle of the line; a short dotted normal is drawn upward from that point, a dotted arc spans from the ray to the normal, and the arc is labelled 18 degrees. The four boxes are identical up to that point. WITHHELD deliberately: what each drawing then does at the interface - the direction each continues in, and at what inclination - because that difference IS the answer and putting it in the option text would hand it over. The option texts are therefore neutral placeholders pointing at the attached crop, following the committed precedent of 55/5/1 Q12(i). The same four drawings are reprinted on the Hindi facing page idx 11; crop from idx 12.
